# Pettifer

## Overview

- **Age:** Elderly  <sub>[v1 c18 P49](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0049)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v1 c18 P4](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0004)</sub>
- **Status:** Married  <sub>[v2 c3 P15](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0015)</sub>
- **Origin:** New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Role:** Farmer  <sub>[v1 c18 P1](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0001), [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** James A.  <sub>[v2 c1 P13](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0013)</sub>

## Appearance

Pettifer is a short, heavy-set, bald elderly man with a round face, bulging blue eyes, and a small strip of hair surrounding his ears.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c1 P12](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0012), [v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049)_

## Personality

He is an eccentric, candid, and short-tempered individual who speaks his mind bluntly. Known for being stingy and stubborn, he prefers to do things his own way and dislikes the intrusion of busybodies or female authority. Despite his crusty and irritable exterior, he possesses a softer, friendly side, enjoys good humor, and appreciates warm companionship.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P8](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0008), [v2 c3 P22](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0022), [v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025), [v2 c3 P43](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0043), [v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049)_

- Farming  <sub>[v1 c18 P1](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0001)</sub>
- Tea-making  <sub>[v2 c3 P33](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0033)</sub>

## Goals

- To keep his farm and crops protected from intruding animals  <sub>[v2 c1 P13](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0013)</sub>
- To live comfortably without unwanted interference from others  <sub>[v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006)</sub>

## History

Pettifer purchased the Robert Bell farm in Brierley and moved there from New Brunswick, quickly establishing a reputation as an eccentric bachelor who kept house alone. He engaged in a feud with Agatha Sowerby after making blunt remarks to her when she solicited donations for missions. Later, he became infuriated when Nell's Jersey cow repeatedly broke into his oatfield, confronting Nell directly. However, after Nell accidentally sold his cow to a buyer, he surprisingly accepted the mistake with humor and agreed to trade cows with her, leading to a warm friendship between them. Soon after, his estranged wife Emily returned to live with him, restoring tidiness to his household. Tragically, his pet parrot Nutmeg was killed by lightning during a severe thunderstorm, which deeply saddened him. Over time, he became a supporter of Nell's Village Improvement Society and maintained his unique, blunt, yet friendly relationship with his neighbors.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c1 P8](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0008), [v2 c1 P13](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0013), [v2 c2 P23](../source/v02-c02.md#nw-v02-c02-p0023), [v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c3 P54](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0054), [v2 c4 P43](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0043)_

## Background by volume

- He formerly resided in Scottsford, New Brunswick, before moving to Brierley.  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- He purchased Robert Bell's farm adjacent to Grey Shutters.  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- He was previously married to Emily, but separated from her due to constant marital squabbles before they eventually reconciled.
- He owned a cursing parrot named Nutmeg, which was gifted to him by his sailor brother.  <sub>[v2 c1 P10](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0010), [v2 c3 P38](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0038)</sub>

## Quotes

> There is nothing wrong with my fence. A demonic cow of that sort could not be contained even by the prison fence.  <sub>[v2 c1 P18](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0018)</sub>

> Bless my soul, do not utter a single further word regarding it. It is immaterial . . . utterly immaterial. Misfortunes are bound to occur.  <sub>[v2 c3 P22](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0022)</sub>

> I’m a crabbed, lonesome, crusty old chap, but I feel young again because of something about that little girl . . . and having that sensation repeated once in a while is something I’d like, since it’s so pleasant.  <sub>[v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049)</sub>

> I was never skilled at making guesses, Mistress Carrow, but even so, upon entering I reflected, ‘Where did I previously encounter those eyes?’—because I TRULY have encountered them.  <sub>[v2 c24 P20](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0020)</sub>
